title: VAV-1 Reheat Valve Commanded But Mechanically Stuck
description: WebCTRL commands VAV-1's reheat valve normally, and the real object shows the new command was received -- but the valve actuator has physically seized, so discharge air temperature never responds.

events.description: AHU-1 supply fan on for airflow to exist at VAV-1
Reheat valve actuator seizes at whatever position it's at right now -- WebCTRL's commands still land on the real BACnet object, the actuator just doesn't move

expected_results: The HW Valve object itself keeps accepting new WriteProperty commands from WebCTRL and shows the commanded value changing
VAV-1 Discharge Temp stops responding to those commands and holds near whatever it was when the fault activated
A student comparing 'commanded' vs 'actual discharge temp' should see the mismatch even though the point looks normal on a quick glance
completion_criteria: Student identifies that the command point and the resulting physical behavior have diverged, rather than assuming the valve command itself is wrong
Student proposes a field verification step (e.g. checking actuator position manually) rather than only re-checking software
instructor_notes: This fault does NOT change what WebCTRL reads back from the HW Valve object -- that's intentional. The point of this exercise is to teach that a healthy-looking command point doesn't guarantee the field device is actually responding.
student_objectives: Distinguish a software/network problem from a mechanical actuator failure using only available BACnet points
Understand why 'the point shows the right value' isn't proof the equipment did what was commanded
